titre: Diablo 4 Officially Gets a Big Live-Service Change
chapo: Diablo 4's 16th season will make a big change to the game’s usual update cadence, keeping much of season 15.
extrait: Season 15 was so popular, some of its best features are sticking around Like many games built around a live-service model, Diablo 4 adds and removes a lot of content each season to keep players coming back as often as possible. However, the game’s next season will be a bit of a departure from that usual formula. On Tuesday, Blizzard revealed a first outline of Diablo 4’s 16th season, titled Season of Tyrael’s Gambit, which will center on the continued battle against the Úllo Sar death cult. It will add new items, rewards, and battles when it releases on Dec. 1. However, beyond the standard new content players have come to expect, Season 16 makes a big change from the game’s typical release cadence: it keeps some of the most popular content added last season. Diablo 4’s 15th season, Season of Hell’s Legacy, was a 30th-anniversary blowout filled with nostalgic throwbacks, especially to Diablo 2. It was very well-received by fans, who enjoyed the iconic returning characters, areas, and monsters it added. Diablo-heads apparently loved it so much that Blizzard is making several features permanent fixtures of the game going forward, something it generally avoids. As for what's staying, the most notable inclusion is the recreation of Old Tristram from previous games and the reincarnated Deckard Cain. Cain’s books can be accessed from a pedestal in town. Beyond this, several boss fights, dungeons, and encounters will remain accessible. The Prime Evil boss fight can now be summoned as a normal Lair Boss; Season 15’s Capstone Dungeons are sticking around and being moved to Torment 10+ difficulty; and the Waking Nightmares dungeons, which are inspired by areas in past games, will remain accessible through Chronicle of Nightmares Dungeons Keys. Several items are sticking around as well, including Legacy Uniques like the Annihilus Seal and Hellfire Torch Charm. Hopefully, this approach of keeping more of the most popular features will become Diablo 4's norm going forward. While many Diablo 4 players were worried about Blizzard’s continued support for the game after the studio announced Diablo 5, the team said that it will continue making content as long as fans keep playing. At least so far, Blizzard shows no signs of slowing down.

titre: Blizzard is making a lot of the Diablo 4's event-specific Diablo 2 anniversary content permanent because everyone loved it in Season 15
chapo: Blizzard has officially unveiled Diablo 4 's next live-service season: Season of Tyrael's Gambit. This is the ARPG's 16th season, and it follows on from the popular and well-received Season of Hell's Legacy. Read more
extrait: Blizzard has officially unveiled Diablo 4's next live-service season: Season of Tyrael's Gambit. This is the ARPG's 16th season, and it follows on from the popular and well-received Season of Hell's Legacy. In an unexpected move, Blizzard announced it's keeping some of the nostalgia-laiden content from the previous season, Season of Hell's Legacy, as a permanent addition. This is unusual, as the ephemeral nature of live seasons means new content goes away at the end of each season. Season of Hell's Legacy paid tribute to Diablo's legacy and its 30th anniversary by introducing a lot of content inspired by previous Diablo games, chiefly Diablo 2. The list includes the return of iconic character Deckard Cain, a recreation of Old Tristram, and a big fight against the three Prime Evils - Diablo, Baal, and Mephisto - in their classic forms. "We heard overwhelming requests for features from Season of Hell's Legacy to carry forward as permanent game features," Blizzard wrote in Season 16's announcement post. "While the entire season couldn't come along for the ride, we are implementing the following features with the launch of Season of Tyrael's Gambit that will carry forward in both Eternal and Seasonal realms." Season of Tyrael's Gambit kicks off 1st December, so you still have time to access all of that in Diablo 4 until Season 15 ends. Certain things, such as craftable items, won't return, so you may as well try them while you can. That said, Blizzard is aware of the love some of those items have, and the developer said it may bring them back in the future.

titre: Diablo 4's nostalgia-heavy season 15 was so good that Blizzard is making a lot of it permanent
chapo: Legacy Uniques, World Boss Diablo summons, and even Moophisto are carrying over into Diablo 4 season 16

Legacy Uniques, World Boss Diablo summons, and even Moophisto are carrying over into Diablo 4 season 16 Blizzard scored a major win with Diablo 4's nostalgic season 15, which coincided perfectly with the series' 30th anniversary and the triumphant return of BlizzCon, not to mention the announcement of Diablo 5. Season of Hell's Legacy pulled many of its headlining features from Diablo 1, 2, and 3, including a questline recreation of the first game's main storyline. The season has been a hit with players, so it made sense when Blizzard confirmed that some of its features would stay in the game permanently. Now, we know which features exactly, and it's clear Blizzard is doubling down on the nostalgia. "We heard overwhelming requests for features from Season of Hell’s Legacy to carry forward as permanent game features," reads Blizzard's announcement of Diablo 4 season 16, now officially titled Season of Tyrael's Gambit. "While the entire season couldn’t come along for the ride, we are implementing the following features with the launch of Season of Tyrael's Gambit that will carry forward in both Eternal and Seasonal realms:" By far my favorite addition in season 15 was the beautifully reimagined Old Tristram, and that'll remain accessible, along with its side quests and Deckard Cain's books, via the portal in the Imperial Library. Real ones will know about Cow Island, a callback to one of the series' most beloved Easter eggs, and that will also remain accessible along with the Moophisto world boss summon. Likewise, the big Uber Diablo World Boss summon is coming along for the ride in season 16, as well as the Annihilus Seal he drops. And speaking of items, the Legacy Uniques from older Diablo games are sticking around, as is the Hellfire Torch Charm, a nod to Diablo 2. Arguably the most notable season 15 feature getting stamped into the game permanently is the Prime Evil Council fight, which puts you up against Diablo, Mephisto, and Baal simultaneously. Blizzard says that battle will work like a typical Lair Boss in terms of summoning and claiming rewards, and that you won't need any materials to access the encounter.
